item.title: Dozens of homes torched in Narail after killing of two BNP leaders
item.description:
Dozens of homes and shops belonging to Awami League leaders and activists were attacked, vandalised and set ablaze in Narail’s Kalia upazila on Friday, in apparent retaliation for the killing of two BNP-affiliated leaders earlier in the week.
The violence swept through Bendar Char village from Friday afternoon into the night, targeting properties associated with the activities-banned Awami League, including the ancestral home of former Narail-1 lawmaker BM Kabirul Haque Mukti and the residence of former Kalia municipality mayor Fakir Mushfiqur Rahman Liton.
The fire service reported fires at approximately 20 to 30 homesteads, with multiple structures in each compound potentially pushing the number of damaged buildings considerably higher.
Police and local administration officials, however, gave lower estimates of between 15 and 20 affected houses.
Residents alleged that people associated with the BNP carried out the attacks, but local BNP leaders denied the accusation.
The violence followed Wednesday’s killing of two BNP-affiliated leaders when a motorcycle procession came under attack at Bot Tola intersection in Bendar Char.
The victims were identified in local reporting as Shaheen Molla, general secretary of Kalia municipal Krishak Dal, and Sohel Molla, general secretary of the Kalia upazila unit of Jatiyatabadi Samajik Sangskritik Sangstha (JASAS).
Both were critically injured and taken to Kalia Upazila Health Complex before being transferred to hospitals in Khulna, where they were declared dead.
Humayun Kabir, station officer at Kalia Fire Service, said the fires began around 4pm on Friday, but firefighters could not reach the village immediately because trees had been felled across access roads and there were security concerns.
Firefighters arrived around 8pm, when several houses were still burning, although the intensity of the fires had subsided.
He said more than 50 residential structures across approximately 20 to 25 homesteads were gutted. Several shops at Bardia Bazar were also set on fire.
Kalia Upazila Nirbahi Officer Jinnatul Islam, who visited the scene with police, confirmed that 15 to 20 houses had been vandalised and several structures set ablaze, including the former lawmaker’s ancestral home.
Residents also alleged that furniture, valuables and other belongings were looted from affected properties.
In a statement on Saturday, Narail police rejected social media allegations that Hindu households and businesses in Bendar Char had been targeted.
Superintendent of Police Mohammad Al Mamun Sikder said the claims were false and fabricated, alleging that previously recorded and AI-generated videos had been circulated to misrepresent the violence.
Police maintained that there were no Hindu settlements in the affected area and that no Hindu families or businesses had been attacked.
The police statement acknowledged that an agitated group, including relatives of the two slain BNP leaders, had gathered in the village around 4:45pm on Friday and attacked several houses belonging to Awami League activists allegedly involved in Wednesday’s killings.
Police said officers subsequently brought the situation under control and additional personnel were deployed.
Kalia upazila BNP General Secretary SM Wahiduzzaman Milu denied allegations that BNP leaders and activists had organised or participated in the arson attacks.
He also rejected social media claims that more than 200 houses had been attacked.
Police identified Disha Biswas, 31, and Rakib Biswas, 21, as two suspects arrested in connection with Wednesday’s killing of the BNP-affiliated leaders.
Kalia Police Station Officer-in-Charge Idris Ali said no case had been filed over the killings as of Saturday noon.
He said the victims’ families were expected to approach police to initiate legal proceedings.

item.title: 350 tourists return from St Martin’s by trawler, 1,500 remain stranded
item.description:
Around 350 tourists stranded on Saint Martin’s Island due to adverse weather returned to Teknaf by trawler on Saturday, while many others remained on the island awaiting transport.
The tourists left the island aboard 10 trawlers between 8:30am and 12:30pm on Saturday. However, a shortage of trawlers has left many others waiting at the island’s jetty.
The district administration suspended tourist vessel operations on the Cox’s Bazar-Saint Martin’s route from Thursday until further notice due to adverse weather, leaving around 1,000 tourists who had travelled from Cox’s Bazar stranded on the island.
Abdur Rashid, president of the Teknaf-St Martin’s Trawler Owners’ Association, said on Saturday afternoon that many tourists were facing difficulties, with some running short of money.
Considering their situation, arrangements were made to transport tourists to the mainland by trawler from Saturday morning with permission from the local administration, he said.
A total of 350 tourists had returned to Teknaf aboard 10 trawlers, with each vessel carrying 30-35 passengers. Many others were still waiting at the jetty due to the limited number of available trawlers, he added.
Khalilur Rahman, a tourist from Rajshahi, was waiting at the island's jetty with his family. He said they had visited St Martin’s for a holiday but became stranded after ship services were suspended due to bad weather.
What was supposed to be a pleasant holiday had turned into an ordeal, as their travel budget had run out and they were desperate to return home, he said.
Nurul Amin, a beach worker on the island, said many tourists had become stranded due to the suspension of vessel services. Since Saturday morning, 10 trawlers had left for Teknaf carrying tourists, he added.
Fayezul Islam, acting chairman of St Martin’s Union Parishad, said tourists wishing to return were travelling by trawler from the island's jetty to Shahporir Dwip jetty in Teknaf.
Those choosing to remain on the island were staying there, while the others would be able to return to Cox’s Bazar by ship once regular services resumed, he added.
SM Anik Chowdhury, Teknaf upazila nirbahi officer, said some stranded tourists, particularly those facing financial difficulties or other urgent needs, were returning to Teknaf by trawler.
The authorities were keeping track of those still on the island, he added.
According to the district administration, tourist vessel operations on the Cox’s Bazar-Saint Martin’s route began on November 5 this year, with five vessels receiving permission to operate during the current season.
Tourist arrivals have increased since the season began. On November 13, a total of 1,754 tourists travelled to the island aboard four vessels, marking the highest single-day arrival of the season.
On Wednesday, another 1,241 tourists reached the island aboard four vessels: 472 on the MV Baro Auliya , 372 on the Karnaphuli Express , 145 on the MV Teknaf and 252 on the MV Malancha .
Under government guidelines, tourists are allowed to visit St Martin’s Island from November 1 this year to March 15 next year, with overnight stays permitted.
Each visitor must pay an environmental conservation fee of Tk100 and obtain a travel pass and a ticket containing a QR code.
Several restrictions have also been imposed to protect the island’s fragile ecosystem and biodiversity. The use of lights, loud noises and barbecue parties on the beach and surrounding areas at night is prohibited.
Motorcycle and sea-bike operations on the beach, as well as the collection of natural resources from the island, are also banned.

item.title: PM attends reception for gallantry award-winning freedom fighters
item.description:
Prime Minister Tarique Rahman on Saturday attended a reception for gallantry award-winning valiant freedom fighters and their heirs, held to mark Armed Forces Day 2026.
The prime minister joined the program in the morning at the Army Multipurpose Complex in Dhaka Cantonment, his Deputy Press Secretary Jahidul Islam Rony said.
He walked from the Armed Forces Division office in the cantonment to the venue.
The prime minister handed over souvenirs to selected gallantry award-winning freedom fighters and their heirs and exchange greetings with them.
Armed Forces Day is observed every year on November 21 in memory of the day in 1971 when the Bangladesh Army, Navy and Air Force launched a joint offensive against Pakistani forces during the Liberation War.

item.title: Beyond the law: Rethinking human rights through the social sciences
item.description:
On an ordinary day in Kalyanpur in May this year, Md Russel was allegedly abducted by 20 to 25 men after refusing a Tk15,000 monthly extortion demand. They took him into a slum and beat him until locals heard his cries and intervened. Two days later, he filed a police complaint. But instead of investigating, police reportedly urged him to settle the matter with the accused.
For Russel, filing a complaint did not lead to an investigation. His experience raises questions about police discretion and whether people can seek justice without being pressured by those they accused. This one incident cannot represent the entire justice system, but it shows how institutional practices affect people’s ability to exercise their rights.
Like many stories across Bangladesh, this reminds us that human rights violations are not abstract. They are lived, contested, and silenced at the intersection of class, gender, and power.
Understanding human rights requires more than knowing what the law guarantees. We must understand why some can claim those rights while others cannot.
We speak of human rights in legal terms. The Constitution guarantees equality of all before the law, freedom of speech, and protection against arbitrary arrest. Bangladesh is a signatory to major human rights treaties. Rights are framed as legal entitlements to be claimed, defended, or litigated.
Yet, law can tell us what rights exist, but not why some exercise them more easily than others.
Legal anthropologist Sally Engle Merry showed how human rights are reshaped as they move across societies and institutions . Rights acquire meaning through local contexts, social relations, and everyday practices. To understand whether rights are protected, we must look beyond legal documents to see how individuals exercise them.
In the Chittagong Hill Tracts, indigenous communities see land not as property but as ancestral identity. When the state applies land laws designed for flatland ownership, it challenges these cultural meanings.
As Signe Leth of the International Work Group for Indigenous Affairs notes, land is not just a commodity for Indigenous Peoples but a part of their identity, spirituality, and life.
The same gap appears in the experience of the hijra community. Recognition as a third gender in 2013 did not automatically remove the stigma and exclusion that shape access to housing, education, healthcare, and employment.
Changing the law and changing social relations are not the same thing. These examples show how culture and social norms shape rights, a concern central to Anthropology.
Garment workers’ experiences show how workplace hierarchy, gender, and class affect the ability to claim rights. Despite the Labour Act's protections, a 2025 study of 332 female garment workers found that 22$ of workers reported frequent sexual harassment inside the factories during the preceding six months by supervisors, male co-workers, and security guards.
For workers who depend on their wages, fear of job loss and retaliation can make formal protection difficult to claim. Applying a sociological lens shows that while a right may be guaranteed by law, whether someone can exercise it depends on their social circumstances.
Human rights also depend on institutions capable of enforcing the laws. A UN fact-finding report on the July-August 2024 violence in Bangladesh documented how weak internal oversight and barriers to prosecuting public officials hindered accountability. When complaints are handled by institutions implicated in abuses, victims may have little assurance of independent investigation or meaningful redress.
Finally, understanding human rights requires looking at the material conditions of freedom. When a child in a coastal village loses access to school due to flooding, or when a family is displaced by river erosion and cannot recover their livelihood, the problem is not just environmental or economic. It affects their ability to exercise basic rights.
A BIGD study of social assistance in Satkhira found that beneficiary selection could be shaped by kinship networks, political affiliation, gender, religious identity, and proximity to local representatives, despite formal eligibility criteria.
Economic vulnerability can also make travel, paperwork, legal support, and time away from work difficult to afford. Amartya Sen’s capability approach reminds us that freedom is not merely possessing a right, but having the real opportunity to use it.
Across these examples, rights are shaped by more than laws. They are shaped by the institutions people encounter, social hierarchies they live within, and the resources available to them.
If law is the pillar of rights, social science is its foundation. Each discipline offers a lens: Law defines rights and duties, anthropology reveals cultural meanings, sociology exposes inequality and social hierarchy, political science examines institutions and power, and development economics shows how material conditions affect freedom. Together, they reveal what a strictly legal lens cannot explain.
Bangladesh has made progress, from women’s participation to digital access. Yet persistent inequalities, gender-based violence, institutional weakness, and social exclusion remind us that rights cannot be legislated into existence. They must be supported by social and institutional change.
That includes complaint and redress mechanisms that protect complainants, stronger institutional oversight, and fewer financial and social barriers for marginalized groups.
Interdisciplinary research can strengthen rights protection by showing where rights on paper fail in practice and by involving affected communities in judging whether reform works.
Sanjid Tahsin Rakin is a research associate at the Brac Institute of Governance and Development (BIGD), Brac University.

item.title: Grameen Bank branch torched in Tangail's Nagarpur
item.description:
A branch of Grameen Bank in Nagarpur upazila of Tangail was set on fire after miscreants allegedly poured petrol inside the office late Friday night.
The incident took place at the bank's Goyhata branch. The attackers are believed to have opened a ground-floor window, poured petrol inside and set the office ablaze.
A plastic bottle and burnt pieces of cloth were found at the scene. Police and local BNP leaders visited the spot after being informed of the incident.
According to police and Grameen Bank sources, the bank's officials and employees had left the office after completing their daily activities. The fire broke out sometime during the night, damaging furniture and important documents inside the branch.
Harizur Rahman, manager of the branch, said he rushed to the office and brought the fire under control after being alerted by the bank's night guard.
Nagarpur Police Station Officer-in-Charge Zahurul Islam said police visited the scene after receiving information about the fire.
He said members of the activities-banned Awami League were initially suspected of carrying out the attack to create unrest in the country. A case was being prepared in connection with the incident, he added.
Earlier, two other Grameen Bank branches in Basail and Delduar upazilas were set on fire in separate incidents on Tuesday night and early Wednesday.

item.title: From Bhasan Char to Leipzig: The hidden lives of sand
item.description:
An exhibition in Leipzig, Germany, is exploring the social, political and environmental significance of sand and silt across four coastal regions, including Bangladesh’s Bhasan Char, through a combination of anthropological research and contemporary art.
Titled Porous Grounds , the exhibition brings together fieldwork by the S.AND – The Future of Coastal Cities in the Indian Ocean research group and artworks examining how sand and other granular materials shape human lives, coastal environments, infrastructure and economies. It is being held from November 8 to December 19, 2026, at KV – Verein für zeitgenössische Kunst Leipzig.
The exhibition is organized jointly by KV – Verein für zeitgenössische Kunst Leipzig and the S.AND Research Group, which is based at the Max Planck Institute for Social Anthropology in Halle, Germany, and funded by the German Research Foundation (DFG).
Since 2023, the research group has conducted anthropological fieldwork along coastlines in Bangladesh, India, Kenya and France. Led by Lukas Ley, the group includes researchers Tarini Monga, Teresa Cremer and Javed Kaisar, who examine the social, political, economic and environmental dimensions of sand, silt and other granular materials.
Each researcher focuses on a different coastal region. In Marseille, France, Ley investigates sediment management, coastal erosion and the political decisions surrounding the treatment of dredged materials. His research examines how scientific and administrative processes determine whether sediment is considered usable, contaminated or dangerous.
In Goa, India, Monga explores how urbanization, coastal infrastructure and sediment management are transforming land use, ownership and access to shared resources. Her work also examines how changes to river and coastal landscapes affect local communities.
In Mombasa, Kenya, Cremer traces sand from extraction sites to urban markets and construction depots. She investigates its role in the city's economy, labor relations, livelihoods, coastal protection and urban development.
In Bangladesh, Kaisar studies the changing coastal chars, particularly Bhasan Char, and how the lives of Rohingya people on the newly formed silt island are shaped by land, water and sediment. His research examines the relationship between land formation, state management, humanitarian assistance, livelihoods and the uncertainty surrounding life on shifting coastal terrain.
The research group examines sand not merely as a natural resource or construction material, but as something deeply connected to human relationships, land management, environmental change and political decisions.
Alongside the research findings, Porous Grounds features works by artists and collectives Simone Albers, Field-0, Lara Almarcegui, and Jeewi Lee and Phillip C Reiner. Their works explore the physical and sensory qualities of sand, including its texture, sound, form and diversity.
The exhibition also seeks to connect scientific research with artistic practice and make academic discussions more accessible to wider audiences. It builds on the group's previous seminars, reading groups, public discussions and collaborations with scientists, social workers, architects, designers and artists.
Through these activities, the group explores three central questions: how sand becomes visible, how knowledge about it is produced, and how scientific, artistic and practical perspectives give the same material different meanings.
Ultimately, Porous Grounds invites visitors to reconsider an everyday material that often goes unnoticed despite its importance in construction, coastal protection, urban development and environmental sustainability.
Exhibition details
Javed Kaisar teaches in the Department of Anthropology at Shahjalal University of Science and Technology (SUST). He is currently pursuing his PhD research with the S.AND group at the Max Planck Institute for Social Anthropology in Halle, Germany .

item.title: Dengue: 3 more die, 1,674 hospitalised in 24hrs
item.description:
Three dengue patients died in the last 24 hours till 8am on Saturday, while 1,674 were hospitalised after being infected with the mosquito-borne disease during the same period.
The latest fatalities have raised the country's dengue death toll to 516 this year, according to the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS).
Of the newly-hospitalised dengue patients, 744 were in Dhaka Division, 93 in Mymensingh Division, 255 in Chittagong Division, 227 in Khulna Division, 146 in Rajshahi, 64 in Rangpur Division and 145 in Barisal Division.
According to the report, a total of 171,954 dengue patients have, so far, been hospitalised across the country this year.
So far, 165,864 dengue patients have recovered and returned home after receiving treatment in the hospitals.
A total of 102,861 people were infected with dengue, and 413 people died from the mosquito-borne disease last year.

item.title: Infantino re-election backed by South American soccer bloc
item.description:
FIFA president Gianni Infantino has "unanimous" backing for reelection as head of world soccer from CONMEBOL, the ten-country South American bloc said Friday.
Infantino faced criticism over his aborted plan to allow private investment into the World Cup, but he also retains support from Africa and Asia for his bid to win re-election next March.
Each country has one vote with 211 members and the winner will need to secure at least 106 votes in the ballot scheduled for March 18 in Rabat.
Conmebol has 10, Africa has 54 and Asia 46.
The CONMEBOL statement was made at Barranquilla ahead of Saturday's Copa Sudamericana final between Brazil's Atletico Mineiro and Argentina's Boca Juniors.
CONMEBOL said it appreciated "the leadership of the current FIFA president" and the "positive transformations in football" that he has driven since taking office in 2016.
Having been the sole candidate in 2019 and 2023, Infantino faces two declared challengers: Frenchman Philippe Diallo and Japan's Kozo Tashima.
Infantino has fended off criticism of the enlargement of the World Cup, giving a FIFA peace prize to Donald Trump and -- at the American president's request -- overturning a red card for a US player during the competition.
So Infantino is under severe pressure for the first time, but mainly due to UEFA's reaction to the private investor plan that forced his humiliating climbdown.
UEFA president Aleksander Ceferin has given full backing to Diallo, while Tashima has pledged to restore "integrity" to world football's governing body.
Tashima, who serves on the FIFA Council, stressed his intention to restore trust in the governing body and make transparency and integrity the hallmarks of his campaign.
He said he decided to run after he was incensed by FIFA's shock decision to lift the ban on United States player Folarin Balogun.
In October FIFA confirmed its intention to set up a $6.35-billion development fund for the next four years.
The fund would allow money to be distributed to FIFA's 211 federations as well as to the regional confederations after a commercially successful 2026 World Cup.
The plan would allow for the payment of $25 million to all 211 member federations.

item.title: Pochettino vows to 'build something' at struggling Man Utd
item.description:
Mauricio Pochettino said Friday that the Manchester United job was too big to turn down as he vowed to "build something" at the fallen Premier League giants.
The Argentine left his role as USA coach to take on the daunting challenge of reviving United's fortunes after Michael Carrick was dismissed last week with the team in the relegation zone.
Former Tottenham and Chelsea boss Pochettino faces a baptism of fire with a trip to bitter rivals Liverpool on Sunday.
The new United manager was upbeat at his first press conference, choosing to focus on the future rather than criticising United's underperforming players.
"We are here not to denounce things," said Pochettino, who has signed a two-and-a-half-year deal at Old Trafford.
"We are here to build something with our players and with the club and try to perform and win games."
United's fortunes have plummeted in the 13 years since Alex Ferguson retired but Pochettino said the job remained a huge draw.
"A club like Manchester United you cannot turn down. You cannot say no," said the 54-year-old, who won the French league title with Paris Saint-Germain.
"It's difficult to find another club, the size of club, that is Manchester United."
Carrick led the Red Devils to third place in the Premier League last season during a successful interim spell in charge but this season has been a disaster.
United are in the bottom three with just one win in their opening 10 league games -- their worst start to a top-flight campaign for 40 years.
Pochettino believes he has inherited a talented squad, despite their current predicament.
"Our most important job is to try to get the best from them," he said. "To create the environment for them to express their talent because we have talented players on the squad. That is our main focus."
- 'Right time' -
Pochettino confirmed that Bruno Fernandes would remain as captain even though the Portugal midfielder's future at the club is uncertain.
Fernandes questioned Carrick's tactics following a 4-1 Champions League thrashing by Como last month and was dropped for the following game.
Last season's Premier League player of the year is out of contract in June, although United have the option to extend his deal by a year.
"Bruno is our captain and I think he is a very important player," said Pochettino. "But all the players need to feel that they are important from the top to the bottom."
United's under-fire CEO Omar Berrada believes Pochettino can kickstart a revival, though he admits sacking Carrick was a "very difficult decision".
"He has a tremendous amount of passion and energy," Berrada told Sky Sports. "We see it already in the two days he's been with us.
"I think he's coming just at the right time for him and us to be able to help the team and take us forward."
Berrada defended the club's signings in the summer transfer window after defender Lisandro Martinez publicly criticised the hierarchy for a lack of investment.
United signed midfielders Carlos Baleba, Youri Tielemans and Andrey Santos but failed to address shortcomings in attack and defence.
Berrada insisted the club remained in the market for "top talent" despite reportedly being priced out of some of their prime targets.
"We have the ambition to win -- to win the Premier League, to win the Champions League, to win the domestic cups and for that, we need top talent," he said.
"When we find the right opportunities, we will spend. But what we don't want to be doing is spending just for the sake of it."

item.title: Cummins wins Cricket Australia's 'unanimous support' to remain Test captain
item.description:
Cricket Australia threw its "unanimous support" behind Pat Cummins to remain Test captain Saturday, rejecting any suggestion his integrity had been compromised by the lingering "Sandpapergate" scandal.
Cummins has been under huge pressure since Usman Khawaja claimed the whole team knew about the plot to alter the ball in a Test at Cape Town in 2018.
He strenuously denied being aware of what was going on in a press conference last week, but his position was undermined when Cameron Bancroft backed Khawaja's version of events.
Only then-captain Steve Smith, his deputy David Warner and Bancroft -- who used the sandpaper -- were found to be responsible by a Cricket Australia probe.
With speculation over Cummins' future rampant and a home four-Test series against New Zealand next month, CA moved to stamp out any further discussion about the 33-year-old's fate after meeting him to check on his welfare.
It came after Josh Hazlewood earlier Saturday suggested he could quit if any action was taken against his long-time bowling partner.
CA expressed "its unanimous support for Pat Cummins as captain" following a board meeting.
"We are absolutely determined to steward Australian cricket through this very difficult time with diligence and patience and to listen and learn," said chairman David Boon.
"We've expressed our support to Pat and our concern for everyone impacted by the events of the 2018 tour of South Africa.
"We have learned from that experience and are proud of the team and the culture Pat and other leaders in the team have fostered over the past eight years and unequivocally reject any implication that Pat's integrity has been compromised."
The retired Khawaja reignited the controversy in his autobiography, alleging the whole team was in the know, and he was strongly backed by close friend Warner.
After Cummins' denials, Bancroft dropped a bomb in a newspaper column by also claiming "it was the whole team" while saying he felt "angry and betrayed" by the Test skipper.
Cricket Australia has ruled out reopening its investigation but instead set up a forum for players to share their experiences about 2018.
- Great leader -
Cummins said being captain "carries with it an awesome responsibility. I have and never will take that lightly".
"David and Todd (Greenberg) have a very tough job navigating cricket through all of this and I commend them for reaching out to me and to many of the players and staff from 2018," he added.
"I support the forum 100 percent. I will be there. All of the players and staff I have spoken with are very keen to go and to have their say.
"There will be a lot of difficult conversations but that is what's needed. Otherwise, from this point, captaining the Australian team in Perth (at the first Test) will be my focus and priority."
Hazlewood threw his support behind Cummins earlier Saturday and made a veiled threat to call it a day if he was removed as captain.
He reiterated that the bowling group at the time, which also included Mitchell Starc and Nathan Lyon, were not part of the plan.
They jointly released a statement in 2021 denying any involvement.
"I want to back Pat and everything he said in his press conference last week, everything he's done for the last five or six years in particular as captain," Hazlewood told the Sydney Daily Telegraph in his first comments since the story blew up.
"He's a great leader. If you went around and asked everyone in the team, you'd hear the same response."
Asked if he would consider quitting in protest if Cummins was removed, Hazlewood said: "I think I'd have to be put in that position to make a decision, but you'd have to think about it, yeah."
Starc has also reinforced that he knew nothing in recent days. Lyon and Smith have yet to comment.

item.title: Alcaraz brushes off injury to down Cobolli at ATP Finals, Medvedev advances
item.description:
Carlos Alcaraz made light of any potential hamstring issues he may be facing as he eased to a 6-4, 6-1 victory over Flavio Cobolli in the ATP Finals on Friday, in the process booking a last-four meeting with Ben Shelton.
Russia's Daniil Medvedev later battled past American Frances Tiafoe 6-3, 6-4 to snatch the final last-four berth and set up a clash with world number one Alexander Zverev on Saturday.
Third seed Alcaraz had an MRI scan on the thigh issue on Thursday but showed little sign that the heavy strapping on his left leg was hampering him as he needed just over an hour to dismiss the world number six in Turin.
With three victories from his three Ivan Lendl Group outings, Alcaraz has topped the pool and will face American Shelton on Saturday in a repeat of the Paris Masters final earlier in November.
Alcaraz beat Shelton 7-6 (7/5), 7-5 in the final in France to win the title for the first time, a measure of revenge on the American who had ended the Spaniard's US Open title defence earlier in the season.
"The challenge is not on the court now, it's outside the court," the 23-year-old Spaniard said.
"I will do everything to be in better shape, physically, to be ready tomorrow (Saturday). It's going to be a really important half of the day that I have ahead of me with my team, with my physio.
"So we will see, but I think I'm doing great things. I felt great on court today."
Medvedev reached the ATP Finals semi-finals for the fourth time and first since 2023.
Both Medvedev and Tiafoe had beaten Cobolli but lost to Alcaraz earlier this week in the Ivan Lendl Group, leaving a winner-takes-all clash between the two.
A missed backhand slice in the first set gave Medvedev the crucial break of serve, before Tiafoe lost his serve once again at 4-4 in the second set.
Tiafoe saved three break points in the ninth game, but the seventh seed was unable to hold off Medvedev who served out for his 54th win of the season.
Fourth-seed Medvedev is bidding for his fifth title this season and his second ATP Finals crown after 2020.
- 'Dream come true' -
Alcaraz has not lost a match going back to a round-of-32 exit at the Shanghai Masters in early October, and that confidence and form was on clear display as he broke Italian Cobolli in the very first game of the match.
The seven-time Grand Slam champion served out the opener,
before again breaking the 24-year-old in the first game of the second set before racing to victory.
"It was a difficult match for me, because I had to see how I was going to feel on the court," Alcaraz said.
For French Open runner-up Cobolli it was a swift and painful end to his Finals debut as he finished bottom of the group with three defeats in as many outings.
"When you're here, everything is fantastic, and it's a dream come true," said the Italian.
"Of course I'm very proud of myself, of my team, and the goal now is to come back next year."

item.title: Kane ankle injury blow as Bayern held by Cologne
item.description:
Bayern Munich striker Harry Kane is set to miss several months with an ankle injury sustained in a bruising 1-1 home Bundesliga draw with Cologne on Friday.
Kane was subbed out early in the match and Bayern confirmed the England captain would be out for an extended period.
Bayern issued a statement confirming Ballon d'Or winner Kane would be sidelined for "the next few months" due to a torn ankle ligament.
Sporting director Max Eberl told reporters club doctors were "currently discussing whether or not to recommend surgery".
Tottenham loanee Mikey Moore scored for Cologne before Kane's injury but Bayern levelled things through Nathaniel Brown before the break.
France winger Michael Olise also went off injured after a tackle late in the first-half.
Said El Mala had an excellent late chance to snare a first Cologne win at Bayern since 2009 but he pulled the ball just wide with the goal beckoning.
Now a point behind Bayern, chasers Borussia Dortmund can move into outright first on the table if they win at Borussia Moenchengladbach on Saturday.
"We started well, but then we had the injuries to Harry and Michael. Still, no excuses -- Cologne deserved it. And to be honest, we have other concerns right now," Bayern coach Vincent Kompany told Sky Germany.
Bayern are in currently in the midst of an injury crisis, particularly up front.
Jamal Musiala, Luis Diaz, Ismael Saibari, Serge Gnabry, Alphonso Davies and captain Manuel Neuer have all missed matches recently.
Despite leaving the stadium on crutches, Olise's condition is believed to be less serious.
"It's just a precautionary measure, I believe," Kompany said. "I'm hopeful Michael will be back Monday."
Despite the draw Bayern, who play away at Lille in the Champions League on Wednesday, remain the only undefeated side in Europe's top-five leagues in all competitions this season.
- Kompany returns -
Kompany returned to the dugout with his arm in a sling, having dislocated his shoulder when he collapsed on the training pitch before being hospitalised with meningeal irritation in October.
Cologne, who arrived in Munich with just one league victory this season, took a surprise lead with 12 minutes gone when Moore started and finished an excellent counter-attack.
Moore pounced on a mislaid Olise pass and drove forward, finding Linton Maina who laid off for El Mala.
With Bayern's defence closing in, El Mala stroked a no-look backheel in Moore's path and the Spurs loanee coolly rounded goalkeeper Jonas Urbig and slid the ball home for his first Bundesliga goal.
Bayern went on the attack immediately but suffered another setback when Kane was brought down in the Cologne box from behind by defender Joel Schmied.
Having his penalty appeals waved away, Kane rose gingerly and tried to continue, but was visibly limping and was subbed out soon after.
Kane, 33, has a history of ankle complaints although he has only missed a handful of games since moving to Bayern in 2023.
The hosts suffered another blow in the dying stages of the opening half when Olise went down under a challenge.
Sensing a first victory over Bayern since 2011 -- a run of 23 games including 21 defeats -- Cologne continued to push, with El Mala and Maina forcing a spectacular double save from Urbig just before the hour mark.
El Mala had a golden chance to put Cologne in front with eight minutes to go when one-on-one with Urbig but cut his close-range shot inches wide of the post.
"I think you can see in my face -- it's unbelievably painful," said El Mala of his miss.

item.title: Bangladesh eliminated from AFC U17 Asian Cup qualifiers
item.description:
Bangladesh U-17 national football team eliminated from 2027 AFC U-17 Asian Cup qualification when they suffered a 2-0 defeat to host United Aram Emirates (UAE) in their ultimate group match held Friday night at Emirates Football Club Stadium, Ras Al Khaimah.
Syria's emphatic 10-0 victory over Bhutan in Friday's opening match officially confirmed Bangladesh's exit from the tournament. Bangladesh had hoped to end their campaign with a consolation victory in their final match. However, that hope also shattered through the defeat to UAE, bowing out of the tournament on a frustrating note.
The AFC U-17 Asian Cup Qualifiers are being held across seven groups, with only the group winners securing a place in next year's final round.
Bangladesh were drawn in Group C alongside UAE, Bhutan, Macau and Syria. Both the UAE and Syria finished the group stage with ten points each, but Syria clinched the group title by virtue of better goal difference.
Earlier, Bangladesh began their campaign with a 5-1 defeat to Syria in their opening group stage match but staged a brilliant fight back to register a convincing 4-0 victory over Bhutan in their second group match.
The boys in red and green recorded their second victory in the competition, beating Macau by a narrow margin of 1-0 goal in their third group match to stay third position in the table with six points.

item.title: How many must burn?
item.description:
As of writing this editorial, five people -- including a nine-year-old girl and a fifteen-year-old boy -- are at the National Institute of Burn and Plastic Surgery after suffering severe respiratory tract burns in a Thursday night fire at a warehouse in Dhaka’s Mirpur-10.
That we continue to have warehouses packed with highly flammable material inside a residential structure in a densely populated neighborhood speaks volumes about chronic regulatory failure.
For years, Dhaka’s residential areas -- from Old Dhaka to Mirpur -- have been turned into ticking time bombs by illegal commercial storage, chemical depots, and unregulated workshops operating right beneath sleeping families.
Every single inferno follows the exact same tragic script: An avoidable blaze breaks out, innocent workers and children suffer horrific injuries or death, authorities express routine shock, and within days, regulatory enforcement returns to its usual slumber.
The presence of minors among the critically injured also raises urgent questions regarding child labour and basic workplace safety compliance. Storing mounds of combustible garment scraps without adequate ventilation, fire exits, or suppression equipment must be called what it is: Criminal negligence.
The responsibility for this recurring nightmare lies with relevant authorities such as RAJUK, who over the years have continued to display a level of disregard that simultaneously deserves scrutiny. Laws governing zoning, building codes, and hazardous storage exist on paper, yet they are rendered meaningless by weak oversight, bureaucratic inertia, and corruption that allow illegal warehouses to thrive unchecked in residential zones.
We must abandon this reactive, post-tragedy posture and launch an immediate, uncompromising eviction and inspection drive across Dhaka’s residential neighborhoods. Illegal commercial warehouses and flammable storage facilities must be sealed immediately, building owners and operators held criminally liable for safety violations, and strict zoning boundaries enforced without exception.
Citizens should not have to live in constant fear of being burned alive because regulators refuse to do their jobs.

item.title: Trump calls for Nvidia’s Huang to be given ‘second chance’
item.description:
US President Donald Trump on Friday called for chip giant Nvidia to reinstate disgraced former CEO Jensen Huang after he resigned over extramarital affairs, including one with an alleged Chinese spy.
“I would love to see him be back. You have one of the truly most brilliant minds in the world, and where is he going to go?” Trump told reporters.
“I think that I would love to see Jensen be given a second chance.”
Huang resigned last week as chief of Nvidia, a company at the center of the AI revolution, after revelations of an affair with an alleged Chinese spy who may have funneled restricted chips to that country.
Reports of at least two further affairs emerged after that initial report, with US intelligence said to be aware of the possibility of the alleged Chinese espionage.
Trump defended Huang as “a good man” who “made some bad decisions.”
“I’d like to see Jensen make a big apology and go back because he created something with Blackwell,” he said, referring to the most advanced chips designed by Nvidia.
The US president also appeared to directly contradict his own treasury secretary, saying he had spoken to China’s President Xi Jinping about Huang during a summit earlier this week.
“I did discuss that with President Xi, and he said, ‘Oh, brilliant, brilliant! He’s a brilliant man,’” said Trump.
Earlier in the day, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said Trump had not discussed Huang with Xi during the meeting in Shenzhen.
Trump advocated for Nvidia to take back Huang as their CEO “if they were smart.”
Huang has offered to return to the company, a move the chip giant’s board has rejected.
Board chair Harvey Jones said in an earnings call this week that “the Nvidia board unanimously accepted his resignation and does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO.”
Earlier, Bessent had spoken at length about the AI race with China in comments to US broadcaster CNBC.
Speaking about the Trump administration’s support for the domestic AI sector, Bessent stressed that the United States “must stay ahead” of China in that realm.
“Our best protection against the foreign SI and exploits by foreign actors is for our labs to maintain their substantial lead, and in effect, they are our shield against SI,” he said, using the government’s preferred SI, or “super intelligence.”
“There’s no turning back on this. What we have to do is make sure that our labs maintain their leads through their continued innovation, through their access to the best chips, and through smart policy.”
Bessent said Trump and Xi had agreed on certain guardrails on the use of AI in the military domain.
“President Trump and President Xi agreed that humans should always be involved in any military decisions that SI makes, and the SI should not be allowed to be autonomous for major military actions,” he said.
On the threat of AI-enabled cyberattacks, Bessent again stressed that the best defense his country had was to allow its AI companies “to continue at the frontier and to provide us with the best defense against these other models.”

item.title: Grand Theft Auto VI takes record $3.8 bn on first day
item.description:
“Grand Theft Auto VI” brought in $3.79 billion in retail sales on its first day, publisher Rockstar Games said Friday, calling it the biggest launch for any entertainment product in history.
The figure, based on company estimates of worldwide sales through the end of Thursday, is nearly five times the roughly $800 million that predecessor “Grand Theft Auto V” took in during its first 24 hours in 2013.
It also exceeds the entire box office run of “Avengers: Endgame,” which became the highest-grossing film of all time last month at about $2.9 billion worldwide after a re-release pushed it back past “Avatar.”
Rockstar, a label of New York-based Take-Two Interactive, said the game had sold 32.5 million units before release, a record across all platforms.
“We are incredibly humbled by the response from players around the world,” said Sam Houser, the studio’s founder and president.
The game went on sale Thursday on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S, launching first in New Zealand and rolling out market by market as each reached midnight local time.
The release quickly became a global phenomenon, generating more social media posts than this year’s World Cup, according to monitoring platform Visibrain.
Critics praised the game, which has a score of 99 on review aggregator Metacritic.
Rockstar said that made it the highest-rated game ever.
In a review for The Verge, Andrew Webster wrote that “the game is so good that the outsize hype is the least interesting thing about it.”
Like its predecessors, “GTA VI” is an open-world action game in which players roam freely through a sprawling city, stealing cars, pulling off heists and carrying out missions for criminal gangs.
The story follows Jason and Lucia from a chance meeting during a police stop to a botched robbery that lands Lucia in jail, much of it told through long cutscenes.
Players then take control of Jason, a former soldier doing odd jobs for local gangsters, which range from recovering drug packages dropped at sea to stealing cars and shaking down debtors.
The game is set in Vice City in the fictional state of Leonida, modeled on Florida.
Its busy streets, neon-lit nightlife and beaches are rendered in striking detail, and non-player characters go about their lives whether or not the player is involved.
The game also asks more of players than its predecessors, with fuel levels to watch, a greater police presence and even home repairs to be done.
It features more than 20 radio stations, with artists ranging from Simple Minds to Daft Punk, as well as new podcasts including a true-crime series about Vice City.
This week the game received eight nominations for the Game Awards, which will be held December 10.
Rockstar spent more than eight years developing the title and delayed its launch twice, first from fall 2025 and then from May 2026.
The studio was also hit by a 2022 hack in which stolen gameplay footage was posted online.
The series has long been accused of glorifying violence and crime, with players able to run over pedestrians, sell drugs and shoot at police.
No official release is currently planned in Russia, China, Lebanon or Qatar.

item.title: Foods to include in your diet to stay healthy this winter
item.description:
The body needs extra care during winter, when maintaining a normal body temperature may require additional energy. However, there is no need to compromise on healthy eating habits. Including certain nutrient-rich foods in your daily diet can help keep you nourished and comfortable throughout the colder months.
Here are 10 foods you can add to your winter diet:
Leafy greens, particularly spinach, are highly beneficial during winter. They are a good source of vitamin C, which supports the immune system. They also contain vitamin K, which helps with blood clotting, and vitamin A, which is essential for healthy vision. These vegetables can be enjoyed cooked and served warm.
Root vegetables such as beetroot, carrots, and turnips are widely available during winter. They contain beta-carotene and essential nutrients, including vitamins A and C. These nutrients support immune function and help the body defend itself against seasonal illnesses.
Vitamin C not only supports the immune system but may also help improve mood. Citrus fruits such as oranges, grapefruit, and lemons are well-known sources of this vitamin. Strawberries, mangoes, and kiwis are also rich in vitamin C.
Eating foods rich in vitamin D is particularly important during winter, when exposure to sunlight may be limited. Salmon is an excellent source of vitamin D. Other sources include egg yolks, fortified cereals, milk, red meat, and mushrooms.
Beans and legumes, such as chickpeas, are rich in protein and provide several essential amino acids. They are also a nutritious addition to winter meals and can help maintain a balanced diet.
Soup is an ideal winter meal, particularly when prepared at home or made with low-sodium ingredients. A soup containing 140 milligrams of sodium or less per serving is considered low in sodium. The term “reduced sodium”, however, means that the sodium content has been lowered by only 25%.
Avoid recipes containing excessive cream, beef, and salt. Instead, opt for soups made with chicken broth, vegetable stock or water, and include plenty of vegetables for added nutrients.
Whole grains such as quinoa, oatmeal, farro, bulgur and buckwheat provide protein and dietary fiber. Oatmeal, in particular, makes a nutritious breakfast or light meal during winter. It contains zinc, which is essential for normal immune function, as well as soluble fiber that supports heart health.
Strawberries, blueberries, blackberries and raspberries are rich in dietary fiber and antioxidants. They are also good sources of vitamin C, manganese and vitamin K1, making them a nutritious addition to a winter diet.
Yoghurt is rich in protein and provides essential nutrients such as vitamin B12 and calcium. It is also a good source of probiotics, which help maintain a healthy balance of microorganisms in the gut. Choose plain yoghurt instead of flavored varieties, which may contain added sugar.
Almonds, walnuts, cashews and pistachios contain antioxidants and essential minerals. They can be a healthy snack during winter. However, opt for raw, unsalted, or lightly salted varieties instead of sugar-coated or heavily salted nuts and packaged trail mixes.

item.title: Türkiye to host Bangladesh delegation, eyeing broader cooperation
item.description:
Türkiye will host a 15-member Bangladeshi delegation from November 22 to 28 in a bid to widen bilateral cooperation beyond trade, with talks focusing on education, healthcare, science and technology, and public administration.
Economic Relations Division (ERD) Secretary Shahriar Kader Siddiky will lead the delegation, which includes senior officials from ministries and government institutions, the Bangladesh office of the Turkish Cooperation and Coordination Agency (TIKA) said in a press release on Saturday.
The Turkish government-backed visit aims to strengthen ties between public institutions in the two countries and give officials an opportunity to exchange experience in areas such as scientific research, technological development and public-sector training, the release said.
In Ankara, the delegation is scheduled to meet officials from Türkiye’s ministries responsible for education, health, trade, and industry and technology. It will also hold talks with the Scientific and Technological Research Council of Türkiye (TÜBITAK) and the Council of Higher Education (YÖK).
The programme includes meetings with the Disaster and Emergency Management Presidency, the Presidency of Defense Industries, the Presidency for Turks Abroad and Related Communities, and the Presidency of Religious Affairs.
The delegation will also meet TIKA President Abdullah Eren to review ongoing development cooperation and explore opportunities for joint initiatives.
After the talks in Ankara, the delegation will travel to Istanbul for visits to cultural and historical sites.

item.title: Police, Hindu leaders reject communal attack claims in Narail
item.description:
At least 30 houses, including those of former Awami League lawmaker BM Kabirul Haque Mukti and Hindu Awami League leader Krishnapada Ghosh, were attacked, vandalised or set on fire in Narail’s Kalia upazila on Friday, while local Hindu community leaders and police rejected social media claims that hundreds of Hindu households had been targeted.
The attacks took place in Bendar Char and nearby areas between Friday afternoon and 8pm, following Wednesday’s killing of two BNP-affiliated leaders during a motorcycle procession.
Although the attacks caused extensive damage to properties associated with the activities-banned Awami League, Hindu residents and community representatives said there had been no widespread attacks on Hindu neighbourhoods.
However, they confirmed that the house of Krishnapada Ghosh, a Hindu Awami League leader and former Kalia upazila chairman, had been attacked in Ghoshpara.
Residents said the affected Bendar Char area has no Hindu settlements, while Ghoshpara, a predominantly Hindu neighbourhood, is located approximately four kilometres away.
Gopi Ghosh, a resident of Ghoshpara, told Bangla Tribune that ordinary Hindu households in the neighbourhood had not been attacked.
“There was no vandalism or arson at our homes in Ghoshpara. No ordinary citizen’s home was attacked,” he said.
He added that residents had received numerous calls after reports of widespread attacks began circulating on Facebook.
Another resident, Biman Ghosh, said no fires had occurred at ordinary households in the neighbourhood.
Baishakhi Ghosh also rejected the circulating claims, saying residents and their relatives had not reported damage to their homes.
Ashok Ghosh, president of the Kalia Puja Udjapan Parishad, confirmed that the house of Krishnapada Ghosh had been targeted but said other Hindu households in Ghoshpara remained unaffected.
He said the attacks in Bendar Char had targeted properties associated with former lawmaker Kabirul Haque Mukti, while no Hindu families lived in that locality.
Arup Ghosh, general secretary of the Kalia Upazila Puja Udjapan Parishad, gave a similar account, saying Ghosh’s house was the only property attacked in Ghoshpara.
Humayun Kabir, station officer of Kalia Fire Service, said firefighters received reports of arson around 4pm on Friday.
He estimated that 25 to 30 homesteads were affected by the fires, which were brought under control by around 8pm.
Other accounts from the fire service indicated that more than 50 individual residential structures across 20 to 25 homesteads had been gutted.
The affected properties included the residence of former Narail-1 MP Kabirul Haque Mukti.
Police, however, put the number of vandalised houses at approximately 20, illustrating differences in the reported scale of damage.
The attacks followed the killing of two BNP-affiliated leaders in Kalia on Wednesday, November 18.
According to police and local BNP sources, a motorcycle procession organised by BNP and its affiliated organisations came under attack near the Bendar Char sluice gate.
The victims, identified in police reporting as Shahin Sheikh, general secretary of Kalia municipal Krishak Dal, and Sohel Molla, general secretary of the Kalia upazila unit of Jatiyatabadi Samajik Sangskritik Sangstha (JASAS), sustained fatal injuries.
BNP leaders accused Awami League activists of carrying out the attack.
On Friday afternoon, relatives of the deceased and other agitated residents gathered in Bendar Char and attacked properties belonging to Awami League leaders and activists allegedly involved in the killings, according to police.
At a press conference on Saturday, Kalia upazila BNP General Secretary SM Wahiduzzaman Milu dismissed social media claims that more than 200 Hindu homes had been torched.
He described the reports as false and baseless, alleging that they were intended to damage the BNP’s reputation.
Milu said party leaders and activists had remained vigilant to prevent further disturbances and maintain communal harmony.
Narail district BNP General Secretary Monirul Islam also rejected allegations of widespread attacks on Hindu households, while acknowledging that some isolated incidents had occurred.
He said the party was committed to protecting residents and their property.
Kalia Police Station Officer-in-Charge Idris Ali said social media reports of attacks on Hindu homes in Bendar Char were false.
He said the locality had no Hindu settlements and alleged that previously recorded footage and AI-generated images and videos were being circulated to misrepresent the violence.
Police accused activists of the activities-banned Awami League of spreading the material to damage the image of the government and the country.
The authenticity and origin of the disputed social media material have not been independently established.
Idris Ali said relatives of the slain BNP leaders and other residents had vandalised around 20 houses associated with Awami League activists on Friday.
He added that some properties had previously been damaged and abandoned following the political upheaval of August 2024.
Police later brought the situation under control and deployed additional personnel to prevent further violence.
Authorities said the situation in Kalia had returned to normal by Saturday.

item.title: Muhit: Sirajganj to be country's first cataract-free district in two years
item.description:
State Minister for Health and Family Welfare Dr M A Muhit has announced plans to transform Sirajganj into the country's first cataract-free district within next two years, with at least 50,000 free cataract surgeries to restore eyesight of 26,000 visually impaired people in the district.
"This special initiative has been taken to make the birthday of Prime Minister Tarique Rahman memorable. The main objective of the program is to present the Prime Minister with a cataract-free Sirajganj district on his birthday on November 20, 2028," he said.
The state minister made the remarks while addressing the inaugural ceremony of a massive eye health program in Sirajganj on Saturday, said a press release.
Prof MA Matin Memorial Eye Hospital is organising the program with a joint initiative of the government and the private sector. The district administration, police administration, Bangladesh Ophthalmological Society and various international organisations are extending support to the initiative.
Referring to the recent situation in the country, Dr Muhit said, "We are taking eye lenses and healthcare services to people's doorsteps, while fascist forces are moving around with machetes and axes to launch attacks and vandalize their own houses and shops.”
He said, "This is the fundamental difference between an elected democratic government and unelected forces." Noting that a survey has found that around 33,000 people in Sirajganj are visually impaired, he said, of them, eyesight of 26,000 people can be restored through cataract surgery.
"To achieve this target, more than 2,000 surgeries will be performed every month over the next two years," he said, adding that eye camps also would be organised in every union of the district under the program to screen eyes of 500,000 to 600,000 people.
At the same time, he said, 300,000 to 400,000 people would be provided with necessary spectacles free of cost.
Stating that widespread corruption and mismanagement had taken place in the health sector during the previous (Awami League) government, he said. After assuming office, the present government has ensured the presence of doctors and the supply of essential medicines at hospitals, he added.

item.title: Boishakhi TV rocked by attack, DMD detained
item.description:
Police took Boishakhi Television Deputy Managing Director and Editor-in-Chief Tipu Alam Milon into custody on Saturday afternoon following a confrontation at the private television channel’s Mohakhali headquarters in Dhaka, where journalists alleged that outsiders attacked and vandalised the office, leaving several employees injured and trapped inside.
The incident, which began around 3pm, reportedly stemmed from an internal dispute over an employee’s resignation.
The situation escalated when a group of outsiders gathered at the office and allegedly attempted to forcibly take away the deputy managing director.
Banani Police Station Officer-in-Charge Salah Uddin said police rescued Milon from a crowd that had surrounded him and took him into custody for his safety.
Police also confirmed that Milon was named as an accused in a murder case filed with Kotwali Police Station in connection with the July-August 2024 anti-discrimination movement.
Officers from Kotwali were subsequently called to the scene to determine the next legal steps.
Speaking to media, the Banani police chief said officers had responded to reports of unidentified outsiders causing disturbances at the television station.
During the confrontation, several journalists and employees broadcast live videos from Boishakhi TV’s Facebook pages, alleging that a group of people had entered the building, assaulted staff and vandalised the newsroom.
Around 3:30pm, a journalist broadcasting from the rooftop said employees were unable to leave the building because attackers had locked the main entrance and disabled the elevators.
“We have just been subjected to an attack by a large mob. Some of our staff have already been injured. We are completely trapped and unable to get downstairs,” the journalist said.
Staff members also alleged that two mobile phones and a camera had been taken during the incident.
Another live broadcast showed an injured journalist receiving first aid inside the office.
Employees said they contacted the national emergency service, 999, seeking police assistance.
Officers from Banani Police Station subsequently arrived and attempted to bring the situation under control.
However, journalists alleged that some individuals continued their attacks even after police reached the premises.
According to a Boishakhi TV employee who spoke to a media on condition of anonymity, the confrontation began after Milon instructed HM Nahiyan, head of the channel’s online department, to resign around 2pm.
The employee alleged that Nahiyan subsequently summoned individuals affiliated with Jatiyatabadi Chhatra Dal and Swechchhasebak Dal, who attempted to take Milon away from the office.
The allegation regarding the involvement of political activists could not be independently verified.
Nahiyan acknowledged to media having a dispute with Milon but gave a different account of how the situation developed.
He said the disagreement arose over the publication of a photo card, following which Milon asked him to resign.
Nahiyan said he requested payment of his outstanding salary and was directed to the human resources department, where the necessary paperwork was prepared.
He said an HR official later informed him that outsiders had caused unrest at the office.
As tensions escalated, employees alleged that a group of outsiders tried to enter the building and forcibly remove Milon.
Police subsequently intervened and took him into protective custody.
The Banani police chief said a murder case linked to the 2024 uprising was pending against Milon at Kotwali Police Station and that officers were examining whether he would be formally arrested in connection with the case.
The incident disrupted operations at the television channel, while journalists appealed for assistance through live broadcasts.

item.title: Dengue plan exists, but implementation lags
item.description:
Bangladesh has a national plan to fight dengue, but its implementation is falling short in almost every area. The plan sets a target of bringing infections below 100 per 100,000 people by 2030. Three years after it was prepared, no significant progress is visible in mosquito control, patient management, disease surveillance or coordination among the institutions responsible.
Meanwhile, 516 people have died of dengue so far this year, according to the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS). That is already more than the 413 deaths recorded in the whole of last year, and the third-highest toll in the country's history of the disease.
In the 24 hours up to November 21, 1,674 new patients were admitted to hospitals. This brings the year's total to 171,954 hospital admissions.
The National Dengue Prevention and Control Strategy was prepared by the DGHS's Disease Control Centre in 2023, as an outbreak was growing. It covers seven years, from 2024 to 2030.
Its priorities include building the skills of doctors, nurses and other health workers, and placing integrated mosquito control under an institutional framework. It also aims to improve disease surveillance and the rapid supply of information, and to strengthen coordination among ministries and agencies. Research and vaccine development are given importance, and a task force is to be formed to monitor progress.
The paper gives detailed instructions on how each initiative should be carried out. Questions remain over how far it has been implemented in the field.
Dengue has been considered a major public health problem in Bangladesh since 2000. In the 23 years up to 2022, about 250,000 people were hospitalised with the disease and around 850 died.
The picture then turned more alarming. In 2023, the country recorded its highest-ever numbers, with more than 321,000 hospital admissions and 1,705 deaths. Deaths fell to 575 in 2024 and 413 in 2025, but have risen again this year.
Public health experts say official figures do not capture the full picture. The DGHS relies mainly on patient figures reported by hospitals. It collects data regularly from 18 government and 59 private hospitals in the capital, and from upazila health complexes, district and general hospitals and medical college hospitals. It does not include information from all private hospitals nationwide.
Many people with fever and other symptoms are tested and treated at home, and these cases are not regularly counted. There is also no guarantee that a death during home treatment will be recorded as a dengue death. This makes it difficult to judge the overall situation from hospital-based data alone.
Public health expert Dr Mohammad Mushtaq Husain said the number of patients outside government statistics could be several times higher. "Many people are receiving treatment at home," he said, and even when someone dies there, the information does not become known. He added that weaknesses in patient management have been discussed for a long time, and that no disease can be effectively controlled without proper management of the disease and its patients.
Dr Husain said the dengue treatment system has still not been decentralised. Patients from different parts of the country must travel to Dhaka, which delays their treatment and puts additional pressure on the capital's hospitals. He said adequate healthcare and patient management arrangements must be ensured at the local level.
Professor Kabirul Bashar, an entomologist at Jahangirnagar University, said infections and deaths are rising precisely because the control strategy has not been implemented. He also said the strategy itself needs amendments, deletions and additions.
In his view, the paper is somewhat weak and not very scientific. He said it was prepared by bureaucrats, with no entomologist involved, and was not based on field-level experience or scientific methods. He said many aspects of dengue control are missing, and called for a new strategy to be formulated scientifically.
Experts also point to a lack of regular, planned activity to destroy Aedes mosquito breeding grounds. Weak coordination between the health department and the local government institutions responsible for mosquito control adds to the problem.
State Minister for Local Government, Rural Development and Cooperatives Mir Shahe Alam said field workers at district, upazila and union levels are carrying out prevention activities in line with the strategy.
He said a national cleanliness campaign is running from September 12 to December 12. Field workers have been told to maintain daily cleanliness, destroy mosquito breeding grounds, renovate 55 canals, apply effective pesticides, and keep hospital beds and kits ready.
He also warned of hefty fines, and cancellation of government flat allocations, if Aedes larvae are found in anyone's home.
Asked why infections were not falling despite these measures, he said: "We are continuing to work from our end."

item.title: SBAC Bank holds Annual Risk Conference 2026
item.description:
SBAC Bank PLC organized its Annual Risk Conference 2026 on Saturday November 21 at the training institute of the bank’s head office in the capital.
Monoar Uddin Ahmed, director, Bank Supervision Department-5 of Bangladesh Bank, attended the conference as chief guest.
SM Mainul Kabir, managing director & CEO of the bank, presided over the conference.
Sheikh Mohammad Mustafijur Rahman, additional director, Bank Supervision Department-5 of Bangladesh Bank, and Major (retd) Abu Fateh Md Bashirur Rahman, member of risk management committee, attended as special guests.
Md Arifur Rahman, joint director, Bank Supervision Department-5 of Bangladesh Bank, and Shagufta Iqbal, joint director, Supervisory Policy and Coordination Department of Bangladesh Bank, delivered speeches as resource persons.
Abdul Quaium Chowdhury, additional managing director of the bank, delivered the vote of thanks.
The bank’s divisional heads, branch managers & sub-branch in-charges participated in the conference through hybrid platforms.

item.title: Prime Bank holds Annual Risk Conference 2026
item.description:
To foster proactive risk culture and support sustainable growth, Prime Bank recently held its Annual Risk Conference 2026 under the theme “Navigating Risk, Securing Value.”
The conference took place at the head office of Prime Bank, the event underscored the bank’s belief that a strong risk culture not only protects value, but also creates it.
Md Faruque, director, Banking Supervision Department-11 (BSD-11), Bangladesh Bank, attended the program as chief guest.
Tania Roksana, additional director, BSD-11, attended as special guest, along with other officials from the department.
From Prime Bank, the conference was attended by the CEO along with the SMT members and other officials of the bank.
Faisal Rahman, chief executive officer of Prime Bank, inaugurated the conference.
He said that in a fast-changing banking environment, the ability to anticipate and manage risk is what lets a bank grow sustainably.
Speaking as chief guest, Md Faruque highlighted Bangladesh Bank’s transition from a compliance-based supervision to a Risk-Based Supervision (RBS) approach.
He emphasized that the central bank and commercial banks must work together to build a sustainable and resilient banking sector.
During their sessions, central bankers discussed key issues related to RBS and the requirements of its effective implementation.
At the event, Prime Bank officially unveiled its new risk management booklet.
Kazi Naim Morshed, head of risk management, presented the bank’s risk management framework, with a focus on identifying risk issues before they become crises.
An interactive quiz and group work made the conference more interactive.
The bank recognized the Top Risk Raisers for strengthening the bank’s risk identification and escalation culture.
In concluding remarks, Md Ziaur Rahman thanked the Bangladesh Bank officials and all participants for their active engagement. He said risk management is everyone’s responsibility across the bank, and that only through this shared commitment the bank truly can navigate risk and secure value.

item.title: NCC Bank inks payroll banking deal with Texpro Eco Apparel
item.description:
NCC Bank PLC has signed a payroll banking agreement with Texpro Eco Apparel Ltd, a premier 100% export-oriented woven and technical apparel manufacturer operating in Birulia, Savar.
Under the terms of the deal, employees and executives of Texpro Eco Apparel Ltd will enjoy dedicated payroll banking accounts, alongside privileged access to retail loans, premium cards, and priority customer support from NCC Bank.
The signing ceremony took place recently at the bank’s head office in Motijheel, Dhaka.
Md Habibur Rahman, deputy managing director of NCC Bank, and Mohammed Tareq Sarker, managing director of Texpro Eco Apparel Ltd, penned the agreement on behalf of their respective organizations.
Also present at the ceremony from NCC Bank were Mohammad Tariqul Amin, SEVP & corporate banking (cluster head-3); AKM Jahidul Alam, EVP & head of operations and process re-engineering; Shahin Akter Nuha, SVP & head of transaction banking and cash management; Mir Tazimul Arefin, corporate banking (unit head, cluster-3); Md Kamrul Hasan Dolon, head of business and branch, Dhanmondi Branch; Anayet Al Mamun, head of payroll banking; and Liman Debnath, senior relationship manager, corporate banking.
Texpro Eco Apparel Ltd. was also represented by Md Farhad Talukder, director (commercial), alongside other senior officials from both organizations.
